Definition: from νάω or νέω (to float); a boat (of any size):--ship.
BiblicalUsage: Where two seas meet, the ship runs aground, and the forepart sticks fast while the hinder part is broken by the violence of the waves.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the ship in Acts is the picture of every plan that runs on without God: the front holds fast and the back breaks apart, and only the promise keeps the crew alive.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
